source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 295,785 square feet, making it the fourth largest campus in Texas by disclosed power.

The 36 MW is a single figure for three buildings, SAT2 through SAT4. It is not broken down by building, and no rack count or tenant is named. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW is roughly 900 racks. At 100 kW per rack, a denser liquid-cooled assumption, it is roughly 360 racks. Both are arithmetic on an assumed density, not a CyrusOne claim, and the operator publishes no density of its own. The gap between those two numbers is the whole uncertainty: the same power supports very different amounts of compute depending on how densely it is packed.

The certifications describe what workloads the campus can host, not who is inside it. PCI DSS covers payment card data, HIPAA covers protected health information, ISO 27001 covers an information security management system, FISMA covers federal information systems, SSAE 16 Type II covers controls relevant to financial reporting, and TIA-942 covers telecommunications infrastructure design. None of them identifies a customer, and the spec page does not either.

The ranking rests on a small published subset. Texas has 137 mapped facilities, but only 19 publish a power figure, and those 19 total 475.41 MW. Most of the state's mapped capacity is invisible to this comparison, so 36 MW is a meaningful share of what Texas has disclosed rather than of what Texas contains. The data does not say how the remaining 118 facilities are powered, whether this campus is expanding, or how its 36 MW is actually used.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
